chunk_findings.detail: `add` treats an already-declared kind as success and never applies the new row. Given `flow.x` already present from `_declared()`, `add("flow.x", args)` with `--text reason` (or a new `--field` / `--lookup`) skips the `EVENTS / owner.toml` write, writes nothing when the fragment already exists, and returns `[]`. The requested redaction or schema change is dropped with no `SystemExit`, so the operator is told the edit was applied while `text`/`fields`/`lookup` stay at the old declaration.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/event_kind.py:153

chunk_findings.detail: `_row` writes `text` and `lookup` names that are not keys of `fields`, despite the contract that every such name must be a field and despite the docstring that a refusal happens before any write. `event_kind add new.kind --why "<at least MIN_DOC chars>." --field holder=str --text reason` emits `fields = { "holder" = ["str"] }` and `text = ["reason"]` and `add` appends that block to the owner toml. The published recipe then rejects the file the scaffold just created (or, if load does not reject it, redacts a name that is not in the field schema).

chunk_findings.detail: `_row` validates `args.checked` with a regex (`re.fullmatch(r"[a-z_][a-z0-9_.]*", args.checked)`), but `add` never adds `args.checked` to the written `[[kind]]` block or the generated TOML output in `reg`. Because `_row` returns `lines` containing `checked = ...`, but `add()` ignores the return value of `_row()` entirely (calling `_row(kind, args)` solely for validation side-effects and then discarding its result), passing `--checked` on the command line validates the format of the argument and then silently drops the `checked` property from the generated TOML file. Given input `python scripts/event_kind.py add foo.bar --why "Test event kind with enough length." --field id=str --checked items.task_add`, line 181 returns successfully, but the resulting TOML file created in `ddflow/templates/events/foo.toml` does not contain the `checked` field.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/event_kind.py:181

chunk_findings.detail: `add` is no longer safe to retry after a partial write. It validates, then appends the `[[kind]]` block, then writes `unreleased/event_kind_added.<kind>.toml`. If the registry write succeeds and the fragment write then fails (missing `FRAGMENTS` dir, permissions, disk full), a second `add` hits `if kind in by_name` and raises `SystemExit` before creating the fragment. `lacks` still reports `fragment: no unreleased/event_kind_added.<kind>.toml`, and the tool has no other writer for that file. The old `_declare` skipped an existing registry row and still wrote a missing fragment; this path cannot repair that tree.

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier probe does not answer this: the test is unchanged and still never runs a writer. Given a throwaway toml under `tmp_path`, it only calls `EK.load_dir()` / `EK.load_dir(tmp_path)` and then compares `FIXTURE`, `log.py`, `test_coherence_coverage.py`, `coherence_exempt.py` and `model.py` to a pre-read byte snapshot. Those calls cannot rewrite those files, so the compare stays green even if `scripts/event_kind.py` add/regenerate still rewrites the fixture, redaction table or coherence lists. The other tests only pin that the current tree already matches `load_dir()`; they do not execute the add path against those shared files.
